lean.fidelity_note: Both statements assert existence of smooth odd divergence-free data $u_0$ on $\mathbb T^3$ and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution $u,p$ on $[0,T_*)$, $0<T_*<\infty$, with uniformly bounded velocity, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and divergent time integrals of the gradient and vorticity $L^\infty$ norms. On every compact set away from the origin, $u$ and $\partial_tu$ converge in every spatial $C^m$ norm. The additional conclusion of Remark 1.2 is that this same velocity extends smoothly in space and time through $T_*$ away from the origin. The formal statement makes maximal-velocity uniqueness explicit. Fields are represented by integer-periodic functions on $\mathbb R^3$, the excluded origin by the integer lattice, and the pressure is normalized to zero mean. The extension is periodic and is not required to solve Euler after $T_*$. The proof uses an auxiliary existence theorem selecting an exponent and a threshold and supplying an extension for all real times away from the lattice. The supplied auxiliary statement file expressly distinguishes this proved existence assertion from the broader auxiliary claim for every threshold satisfying further estimates. The verdict concerns the existential remark, not that broader claim.
lean.name: TorusEuler.Paper.remark_1_2
lean.plain: Smooth velocity extension away from the singularity

statements.markdown: **Remark 1.2.** The solution in Theorem 1.1 may be chosen so that it extends smoothly in space and time through $T_*$ away from the origin. A proof is given in the auxiliary note \[[31](#cite-TerminalSmoothness)\].
